title: No single-source version: a release hand-edits the version in 7+ locations across 6 files, and the drift this invites has already shipped
scenario: Cutting v2.2.1 required manual edits at .claude-plugin/plugin.json:3, .claude-plugin/marketplace.json:13 AND :32, .codex-plugin/plugin.json:3, a new README 'What's new' row (README.md:55), a new CHANGELOG row, and six version references in docs/openai-submission.md (lines 1, 50, 51, 153, 178, 182). CI's validate-plugin job (.github/workflows/ci.yml:40-57) cross-checks only the four manifest fields — and the unguarded surface drifted exactly as predicted: at the v2.2.1 tag, docs/openai-submission.md still says 2.2.0 throughout. Every future release repeats this toil and this risk on the critical path to shipping.
fix: Single-source the version (e.g. .codex-plugin/plugin.json, which package_openai.py already reads at scripts/package_openai.py:123) and add `scripts/release.py bump X.Y.Z` that rewrites the other manifests and stamps README/openai-submission.md; extend the existing CI validate step to grep README and docs/openai-submission.md for the manifest version so any remaining drift fails the build.

title: loop/track engine errors exit 0 — error dicts are printed but never propagated to the exit code
scenario: loopmod.gate()/submit()/wave()/claim() return {"error": ...} (e.g. loop.py:1407 'worker evidence was not submitted', loop.py:1440 'Definition of Done failed'), cmd_loop prints the JSON and falls through to `return 0` (tp.py:772); cmd_track does the same for tr.new/switch/close error dicts (tp.py:1284-1297). A scripted driver (Claude Tag thread, CI wrapper, shell `&&` chain) checks $? , sees success, and proceeds as if the gate passed — while inconsistent siblings (`req score`, `kb lint`, `share push`, `loop verify-dispatch`) DO exit 1 on failure.
fix: In cmd_loop and cmd_track, after computing the result dict, `return 1 if isinstance(out, dict) and out.get("error") else 0` — one check, matching the exit-code convention the other subcommands already follow.

title: Cheap-tier routing is unmonitored by default — nothing observes whether the resolved model ever reaches dispatch
scenario: The tier system resolves models into briefs correctly (loop.py:822-827, lens.py:386-389: sweep=cheap, hard lenses=deep) and even ships a verification hook — but cmd_screen_dispatch returns early unless TASKPLANE_ENFORCE_DISPATCH=warn|strict is exported (tp.py:265-271), and no skill/doc sets it by default. So in the default install a driver that ignores brief["model"] runs the 18-lens sweep and every cheap-marked task on the expensive session model; `loop verify-dispatch` reports only 'no dispatches observed' (taskplane_lite.py:1277-1279). The cost saving the tiering promises is unverifiable exactly where it matters: at dispatch.
fix: Default the dispatch hook to 'warn' (non-blocking systemMessage on mismatch, still zero-cost when models match) and keep 'strict' opt-in; alternatively have `loop retro` surface hook_active=false as an explicit 'tier routing unobserved' cost warning.

title: meter.json read-modify-write is unserialized — concurrent screens lose action counts on the enforced budget
scenario: _meter_bump (tp.py:431-454) does an unlocked _meter_load → increment → atomic-replace. The dispatch queues got _file_lock for exactly this race (taskplane_lite.py:1191-1206) but the meter — which the code itself calls control-plane (tp.py:553-556) — did not. Two governed tool calls screened concurrently (parallel Bash calls in one session, or two agents sharing a workspace) both read actions=N and both write N+1: the enforced max_actions ceiling undercounts and a budget wall of 30 effectively becomes 35+, weakening the one budget that is supposed to be mechanical.
fix: Wrap _meter_bump's load-bump-save in tp._file_lock(meter_path) — the locking helper already exists and the write is already atomic; only the read-modify-write needs the lock.

title: The 'simple front' leaks raw Python tracebacks: main() has no user-layer error boundary (only BrokenPipeError is caught)
scenario: In Claude Tag / team mode the loop state lives in-repo (TASKPLANE_STORE=repo, README v1.4.0). A git merge leaves conflict markers in the state JSON; the user runs `tp summary` (or the skill runs it after a transition) and loop.load() at taskplane/loop.py:155 does a bare json.load() -> json.JSONDecodeError propagates through cmd_summary and main(), dumping a full Python traceback with internal paths at the layer the README (line 22, 'Simple for the user; strict for the agents') promises is simple. No recovery guidance is offered.
fix: Wrap `a.fn(a)` in main() (tp.py:1932) with a catch-all that prints one line to stderr — 'taskplane: <command> failed: <error> (state file <path> unreadable; see tp help / TASKPLANE_DEBUG=1 for details)' — and exit 1; keep the traceback behind TASKPLANE_DEBUG. Additionally make loop.load() raise a typed, message-bearing error naming the corrupt file and the repair step.

title: The fourth promised prompt ('taskplane status') is missing from every Codex discovery surface
scenario: README line 28 promises 'Four prompts are enough' (design / build / review / status), and skills/taskplane/SKILL.md routes all four. But the Codex manifest's defaultPrompt array (lines 35-39) and the submission worksheet's 'Starter prompts' (docs/openai-submission.md:64) teach only three — status is absent. A Codex user who discovers taskplane through starter prompts never learns the one entry point that is guaranteed non-mutating ('What is taskplane waiting on right now?' is even the worksheet's own positive test case 6), so mid-run they poke the loop with build/review phrasing instead.
fix: Add 'taskplane status' (e.g. 'taskplane status — what is waiting on me?') as a fourth entry in defaultPrompt and in the worksheet's starter-prompt list, matching the four-prompt promise.

title: `tp new --budget 0` silently becomes the $3.00 default (falsy check instead of None check)
scenario: `c["budget"]["max_cost_usd"] = float(a.budget) if a.budget else DEFAULT_MAX_COST_USD` — an operator passing `--budget 0` to mean 'no cooperative spend allowed' gets a $3.00 ceiling recorded; `tp status` then shows 3.0 and `tp budget --spent 1` reports under-ceiling.
fix: Use `if a.budget is not None`, and reject negative values explicitly.

title: `lens dispatch --dashboard` re-records dispatch expectations on every re-render — the progress view is not idempotent
scenario: cmd_lens records record_expected_dispatch() for every deep brief and the sweep BEFORE branching on --dashboard (tp.py:826-834). The R1 comment (tp.py:841-846) tells the driver to re-run `lens dispatch --dashboard` after agents land to show DONE lanes — each re-run appends a fresh set of unmatched expectations, so `loop verify-dispatch` reports an ever-growing 'unobserved' count and the dispatch audit becomes noise.
fix: Skip record_expected_dispatch when --dashboard is passed (it is a pure view), or dedupe unmatched expectations by (kind, agent, ref) in record_expected_dispatch.

title: Duplicated git helpers: _git_head clones tp.git_head; _changed_for_impact re-implements changed_files minus the RUNTIME_OWNED filter
scenario: tp.py:_git_head (60-62) is byte-for-byte taskplane_lite.git_head (1051-1053). tp.py:_changed_for_impact (1553-1559) re-implements taskplane_lite.changed_files (636-642) but WITHOUT the RUNTIME_OWNED exclusion and dedupe - so `tp graph impact` (default file set) counts .taskplane/, plan/, knowledge/ bookkeeping as changed files while every loop-internal impact call filters them, giving the CLI a different (inflated) blast radius than the engine computes for the same diff.
fix: Delete both copies and call tp.git_head / tp.changed_files (optionally with an include_runtime flag if the unfiltered behavior is ever wanted intentionally).

title: Bare open().read() without context managers on several read paths
scenario: tp.py:398 (cmd_ready), tp.py:706 (cmd_dod), tp.py:357 (cmd_decision show), tp.py:47 (north_star), loop.py:2364 (_publish_artifacts), kb.py:369 (current_state) and the dashboard's json.load(open(p)) sites open files without `with`, relying on CPython refcounting; on alternative runtimes or exception paths handles linger, and it diverges from the codebase's own dominant `with open(...)` idiom used everywhere else.
fix: Mechanical sweep: wrap each in `with open(...) as f:` - no behavior change, closes the resource on every exit path.

title: `tp summary` prints the same decision sentence twice back-to-back at every gate
scenario: At plan_approval, user_summary sets headline='Decision required — Review and approve the implementation plan.' and decision='Review and approve the implementation plan.' cmd_summary prints the headline (tp.py:1362) and then 'ACTION REQUIRED: Review and approve the implementation plan.' (tp.py:1368) — the identical sentence twice in a four-line output, diluting the scannability of the surface whose whole job is to say the one thing needed.
fix: When a decision is present, shorten the headline to 'Decision required' (progress context only) and let the ACTION REQUIRED line carry the sentence once — or drop the ACTION REQUIRED line when it string-matches the headline suffix.

title: The git hard dependency is honestly documented, but absence degrades to raw tracebacks and every screen event pays a git subprocess
scenario: git is the load-bearing external tool of the whole design (snapshots, DoD diffs, worktrees) and README.md:105 declares it plainly ('Requires `git` in your workspace... Nothing else to set up') - a clean selection rationale. Two rough edges remain in how the dependency is worn: (1) if the git binary is missing, _run's subprocess.run raises FileNotFoundError uncaught, so `tp new`/`tp init`/`tp onboard` die with a traceback instead of the onboarding message the zero-state flow otherwise provides (cmd_screen alone survives via its fail-closed catch-all, tp.py:609); (2) _governed_root shells `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` on EVERY PreToolUse screen event (tp.py:477), an accepted-but-unnamed per-action latency cost of the no-server choice - fine on a laptop, noticeable on slow/networked filesystems.
fix: Catch FileNotFoundError in taskplane_lite._run and re-raise as a one-line 'git is required (see README prerequisites)' error so every CLI path fails with the documented remedy; add a comment at the _governed_root git call naming the per-event subprocess cost as accepted (or memoize the toplevel per cwd within a process).

title: _bare_root hardcodes '/home/claude' - host-specific safety constant with no named rationale or revisit condition
scenario: _bare_root treats exactly `home, '/', '/root', '/home/claude'` as bare roots (tp.py:78-79). '/home/claude' is the Cowork/sandbox session home - a sensible guard given the locked-contract incident - but the list is a point-in-time snapshot of one vendor's container layout, embedded with no comment saying why these paths or when to extend them (another host's session home, e.g. '/workspace' or '/home/user', gets no protection from the exact incident this code exists to prevent). The neighboring lesson block (taskplane_lite.py:884-894) documents the incident thoroughly; the concrete path list it produced is the one part left unexplained.
fix: Comment the provenance ('known agent-sandbox session homes as of v2.x; extend when a host adds one') and/or read extra roots from an env var (TASKPLANE_BARE_ROOTS) so new hosts get the guard without a code change; record the revisit trigger: any new supported host runtime.
